newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on weather, soft cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on weather, soft cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Monday in fairly active trade, pressured all day by a sinking physical market in the face of milder East Coast weather forecasts this week, sources said.
August stumbled 8.3 cents to close at $2.085 per million British thermal units. September settled 8.4 cents lower at $2.058. Most other deferreds ended steady to down 7.3 cents.

"The OTC (over-the-counter) fell apart this morning. We had a lot of lost production back on line today and city gate prices tanked because of the (mild) weather," said one Midwest trader, adding weather forecasts this week were not supportive.
Most pipelines reported gas flows were back to normal after being trimmed by producers late last week because of Hurricane Danny.
While many expected a pullback after last week's rally on the record heat and a hurricane, few expected prices to crater, citing widening cash-to-futures and summer-to-winter spread relationships.

Chart traders now pegged August support at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance this week was seen in the $2.22 area, with further resistance pegged at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices skidded almost a dime to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were off more than a nickel to the $2.05-2.06 area. New York city gate gas skidded 15 cents to about the $2.40 level.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip slumped 4.7 cents to $2.168. NYMEX said 51,751 contracts traded, up sharply from Friday's revised tally of 31,165.

On the KCBT, August finished down 7.1 cents at $2.007, while deferreds ended four to 6.3 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.2 cents to 7.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 441 contracts traded, up from Friday's total of 320.
